# The Bile Lands

*Page PDF 35*

THE TROLL COUNTRY 

## **The Bile Lands**
It should be no surprise how many Stone Trolls stalk the Bile Lands’ stony beaches and craggy cliffs, or that River Trolls haunt its misty fens and secluded bays. It is one of the most hazardous coastlines in the Old World — watch every step. 

Despite typically being loners or convening in trios, Trolls create communal areas known as Bile Pools, which in part give the region its name. Periodically, Trolls must purge their acidic stomach contents, digging holes and hollows in an agreed-upon area to do so. These pools are most dangerous in winter months when the acidic pits freeze over and are hidden under snow. The unwary can lose their legs. 

## **Bile Pools**
Trolls have a habit of eating their victims whole. Sometimes, pools of their vomit contain interesting, if corroded, treasures. Jewellery is unwearable, coins unrecognisable, but metals and gems may be salvageable. 

However, it is dangerous to dip about in a Bile Pool. Anyone doing so must first make a **Hard (–20) Athletics** Test. Failure indicates that they have splashed themselves with acidic goo and suffer a hit that inflicts 11 Damage and a Stunned Condition. Use of tools such as rakes reduces the difficulty to a **Challenging (+0) Agility** Test **.** 

Provided the Character is not _Stunned_ they may then take a **Challenging (+0) Perception** Test. For every SL generated on this Test the Character finds treasure worth 2d10 shillings. 

The Tobol Delta is a huge salt marsh fed by the slowmoving River Tobol. The Ungol-dominated port of Pradeshynya is the first significant settlement along the river and is the furthest most traders venture. The town provides accommodation, warehousing, shops, horsemarkets, and a variety of industries (smithing, tanning, leatherwork, textiles). Come the winter snows it’s even busier, the northern side becoming the encampment of several nomadic tribes. As with the town proper, these are mostly Ungol, with some Gospodar, but also Sarl some years. Most are content to wait out the snows amicably, but conflict does arise. 

Several days’ travel before reaching Pradeshynya, on the northern banks of the Tobol are seen the mysterious Rose Ruins, the crumbled remains of mostly single-storey buildings belonging to a people shorter than Humans, taller than Dwarfs. Among tumbled walls are found many smashed statues, which have defied reassembly into any familiar shape. The Ruins are named for the viciously prickled and creeping roses covering the site. The roses make life difficult for those drawn to the place, mainly archaeologists and treasure-seekers, but also herbalists who believe the rose petals possess unusual properties. 

Nicknamed Orange Keep by non-Dwarfs, Grim is a staging post for Troll Slayers. Built on a low clifftop, it’s a walled compound surrounding a broad, three-storeyd tower. Knowing Dwarfs, it probably has a basement, but no route down is obvious. The Slayers bring home a lot of meat, skins, and furs, which are traded for weapons, warm clothing, food, and ale. Trading ships visit regularly, not only bringing goods, but also more Slayers and other adventurers. The region around Grim is one of the few places you don’t see many Trolls, although warbands attempt sieges every so often, which the Slayers just love. 

## Nominative Determinism?
Chamon Dharek is known for its powerful magical aura, tainted with _Dhar_ . However, perceptive wizards sense zephyrs of Chamon here, too. This phenomenon has become bound to a myth of a sea-witch who could cleave a foe’s ship in twain with a mighty blade. Perhaps there was such a spell, but researchers at the Gold College of Magic in Altdorf have conjectured that the description could refer to a buried artefact — a magical naval ram. It’s possible someone sought to hide this weapon’s magic behind a darker aura. 

## Troll Party
Three Trolls, Shakined Bone Bender, Grog Stuntycrusher, and Hobol Firebreath, are seen together at a communal purging pit. They are getting along famously, laughing, pulling the heads off small animals, and playing catch with one another. In truth they are possessed of a glimmer of intelligence, and Throgg has given them the task of organising the monsters of the western Troll Country into a regiment for his planned army.
